classification.difficultyReason: The hardest part, g, requires reading the separately marked heights, splitting the cross-section into a rectangle and triangle, and multiplying their combined area by the prism length.

content.prompt: Calculate the volume of each of the following solids. For answers involving $\pi$, give the exact value and an approximation correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Rectangular prism with front length 6 cm, depth 5 cm and height 2 cm. Hidden edges are dashed; ordinary source colours are rendered black.
Cube with three edges independently labelled 4 cm; hidden edges dashed.
Right triangular prism, length 18 cm, with perpendicular end dimensions 4 cm and 6 cm. Right-angle marker is at the end's back lower vertex.
spec.mathematics: Cross-sectional area is one half of 4 × 6; prism length 18.

spec.description: Trapezoidal prism with parallel sides 6 cm and 12 cm, perpendicular height 5 cm and extrusion length 4 cm. Single, double and triple equality ticks identify the respective corresponding edges. Parallel arrows appear on the front trapezium's horizontal sides.
Upright cylinder, height 14 cm, with full base diameter 8 cm. Rear base arc dashed.

Half-cylinder lying with rectangular cut face above the curved surface. The 10 cm dimension spans the complete oblique diameter at the left end; longitudinal length is 20 cm. The obscured half of the left semicircular boundary is dashed.
spec.mathematics: Semicircular cross-section radius 5 cm; length 20 cm.

spec.description: Composite rectangular and right triangular prisms extending 12 cm horizontally. Depth is 6 cm. Rectangular height 5 cm and additional triangular height 4 cm are separately dimensioned. Internal horizontal level and right angle at the triangular end are retained.

answer.short:
$504\text{ cm}^3$

Add the rectangular and triangular cross-sectional areas, then multiply by the prism length.
